## Content decision and research brief

The previous qualifying substantive publication completed at `2026-08-29T17:01:17Z` (10:01:17 PDT), so the rolling 48-hour deadline was `2026-08-31T17:01:17Z` (10:01:17 PDT). Waiting until the next scheduled cycle would breach the SLO; a substantive publication was required today after confirming there was no higher-priority product or production defect.

Selected reader problem: **Why does a local Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Cursor session appear or disappear in AgentSight, and what exactly does native session discovery scan/index?**

- Primary implementation evidence: AgentSight v1.0.30 `ext/session/src/parser.rs` and `ext/analysis/src/sources/agent_native.rs`, pinned to product commit `934f441eff8ca210807333633f47b2efcb8cd020`.
- Distinct information gain: provider-owned discovery roots; provider-specific transcript classification and ID extraction; Codex read-only `state_5.sqlite` fast path; bounded 25-row list behavior; cached/lazy transcript hydration; Cursor subagent freshness and duplicate normalization; bounded hydrated detail; implementation-level missing-session failure modes.
- Semantic-overlap audit: `/blog/when-agentsight-works-without-ebpf/` owns the privilege/evidence-mode decision; `/blog/read-agentsight-audit-provenance/` owns row lineage/confidence; `/blog/observe-ai-agent-sessions-in-docker/` owns the named-container bridge. The new page owns local native-session discovery/indexing and troubleshooting, so it is not a keyword variant of an existing article.
- Intended internal links: the no-eBPF evidence guide, audit-provenance guide, and Docker-session architecture guide.
